extension.description: Anti-snipe: a bid inside this many seconds before the end extends the end by this much.

min_increment_bps.description: Minimum raise over the last bid in basis points.

protocol_fee_bps.description: Protocol fee in basis points of the sale price (max 1000 = 10%).

oneOf.description: Escrow note commitment + amount commitment (both hidden) + two FROST group keys.
Close the bid and record its shielded refund. `signature` by `reclaim_vk` (bidder + platform), or none from the bidder once the auction closed or the grace period passed.

Settle to `bid_id`: `signature` by `finalize_vk` (all three parties) over the shielded payment record, and `payment_ref` (zap-1 `app_data_hash`) naming a Confirmed Zcash inclusion of the seller payment at the auction's payment client. Moves the NFT to the bidder.
Optional public disclosure: publish the release OVK (checked against `ovk_tag`) so anyone can decrypt the payment notes and check them against `notes_cm`.
Seller while no bid is active, or anyone after `end_time + reclaim_grace`: NFT back to the seller.

Binary.description:
Binary is a wrapper around Vec<u8> to add base64 de/serialization with serde. It also adds some helper methods to help encode inline.

This is only needed as serde-json-{core,wasm} has a horrible encoding for Vec<u8>. See also <https://github.com/CosmWasm/cosmwasm/blob/main/docs/MESSAGE_TYPES.md>.

HexBinary.description:
This is a wrapper around Vec<u8> to add hex de/serialization with serde. It also adds some helper methods to help encode inline.

This is similar to `cosmwasm_std::Binary` but uses hex. See also <https://github.com/CosmWasm/cosmwasm/blob/main/docs/MESSAGE_TYPES.md>.

commitment.description: blake2b(COMMIT_DOMAIN || auction_id || bidder || escrow_cm || amount_zat || salt).

dkg_transcript.description: Optional hash of the DKG transcript (identifier -> party map), bound in both bind digests so all three parties attest the same share allocation.

escrow_cm.description: Note commitment of the shielded ZEC escrow note, spendable by `reclaim_vk`.

memo_cm.description: `blake2b(memo_preimage(chain, contract, auction_id, bid_index))`, bid_index = the bid id this bid will get. The contract recomputes it.

ovk_tag.description: `blake2b(OVK_DOMAIN || ovk)` of the bid's OVK; every release must use it.

sealed_bid.description: Seller view envelope: `eph_pk || nonce || XChaCha20-Poly1305(ovk, amount, salt)` to `seller_view_pk`, AAD `memo_cm` (see SPEC "seller view").

ShieldedRelease.description: A Zcash payment authorised by a bid group, as recorded on Terp.

notes_cm.description: `blake2b(NOTES_DOMAIN || n || note_1 || .. || note_n)` over the 382-byte SEAM-NOTE-OUT encodings of the payment outputs (see [`notes_preimage`]). Each note carries a random `rcm`, so the commitment hides values and destinations.

ovk_ciphertext.description: The same notes encrypted under the bid's OVK. Opaque on chain.

payment_cm.description: Finalize only: note commitment of the seller's payment output, which the payment client must attest as included on Zcash.

oneOf.description: Active auction for a token, if any.
Open private auction for a token, if any.
The 32-byte digest a FROST group signs for `action`.
Share allocation and thresholds used by private bids.

Addr.description:
A human-readable address.

In Cosmos, this is typically bech32 encoded. But for multichain smart contracts no assumptions should be made other than being UTF-8 encoded and of reasonable length.

This type represents a validated address. It can be created in the following ways 1. Use `Addr::unchecked(input)` 2. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_validate(input)?` 3. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_humanize(canonical_addr)?` 4. Deserialize from JSON. This must only be done from JSON that was validated before such as a contract's state. `Addr` must not be used in messages sent by the user because this would result in unvalidated instances.

This type is immutable. If you really need to mutate it (Really? Are you sure?), create a mutable copy using `let mut mutable = Addr::to_string()` and operate on that `String` instance.

Timestamp.description:
A point in time in nanosecond precision.

This type can represent times from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2554-07-21T23:34:33Z.

## Examples

``` # use cosmwasm_std::Timestamp; let ts = Timestamp::from_nanos(1_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.nanos(), 1_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.seconds(), 1); assert_eq!(ts.subsec_nanos(), 202);

let ts = ts.plus_seconds(2); assert_eq!(ts.nanos(), 3_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.seconds(), 3); assert_eq!(ts.subsec_nanos(), 202); ```

Uint64.description:
A thin wrapper around u64 that is using strings for JSON encoding/decoding, such that the full u64 range can be used for clients that convert JSON numbers to floats, like JavaScript and jq.

# Examples

Use `from` to create instances of this and `u64` to get the value out:

``` # use cosmwasm_std::Uint64; let a = Uint64::from(42u64); assert_eq!(a.u64(), 42);

let b = Uint64::from(70u32); assert_eq!(b.u64(), 70); ```
